1.01.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you take an orthopaedic history?"
- "Personal data, complaint, present history, past, drugs, family, social and function."
- "Analyse every complaint: pain, swelling, deformity, stiffness, instability, weakness."
- "Then red flags; every word must change the diagnosis or the plan."

### The sheet in order
| Part | Ask |
|---|---|
| Personal | name, age, sex, occupation, marital status, smoking |
| Complaint | what, which side, how long |
| Present | onset, course, analysis of each complaint, treatment so far |
| Past | operations, injections, similar episodes, chronic diseases |
| Drugs | steroids — dose and timing |
| Family | similar disease in a relative |
| Social and function | job, daily activities, walking, stairs, sport |

- **Memory:** "**P**lease **C**ome **P**romptly; **P**ast **D**octors **F**ailed **S**ometimes" — the order never changes

#### Why each personal item matters
| Item | Changes |
|---|---|
| Age | type of disease, choice of treatment |
| Manual worker | lifestyle and the type of treatment |
| Smoker | wound healing, bone union, infection |
| Sport | impingement, labral tear |

- Female → DDH (developmental dysplasia of the hip); male → Perthes
- Steroids and alcohol → AVN (avascular necrosis)

### Analyse every complaint
| Complaint | Ask |
|---|---|
| Pain | onset, duration, site, character, intensity, radiation, aggravating, relieving |
| Swelling | when it appeared, growing, painful, changes in size |
| Deformity | when noticed, progressing, the other side |
| Stiffness | small or big joints, rash, how often |
| Instability | giving way, locking, dislocation |
| Weakness | one limb or general |
| Function | walking distance, support, stairs, socks, car, grip |

- **Memory:** pain = **SOCRATES** — site, onset, character, radiation, associated, timing, exacerbating, severity
- **Memory:** complaints = "**P**lease **S**ee **D**octor **S**oon **I**f **W**alking **F**ails"

| Clue | Means |
|---|---|
| Pain after activity | mechanical |
| Pain at night | biological |
| Stiffness | general disease: rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis, lupus |

#### Function scores
- Function questions = items of the joint's outcome score
- Hip and knee: Oxford scores; hand: DASH (Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand)

### Past, drugs, family
- A missed previous operation = a bad exam performance (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Cortisone is often hidden: ask dose and timing; ask diabetes, previous admissions

- Family: same disease in a relative → dysplasia or inherited disease; look at the parents

### Red flags
| Flag | Think of |
|---|---|
| Night pain | infection or tumour |
| Fever, weight loss | infection, tumour |
| Previous malignancy | metastasis |
| Painful scoliosis | spinal tumour or infection |

- Ask every time: trauma, constitutional symptoms, previous malignancy, general diseases (Nagah)
- **Memory:** red flags = "**N**ight, **F**ever, **W**eight, **M**alignancy"
- Settle early: which joint hurts most? Joint or referred pain?

PITFALL — "a long story with no history in it"
- Reading out the patient's story word for word loses the history marks
- Say → "**A 52-year-old manual worker, smoker, with bilateral hip pain for 2 years.**"

1.02.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you examine any joint?"
- "Introduce, ask permission, expose, explain; clues; general examination."
- "Then local: look, feel, move, measure, special tests."
- "Finish with neuro, vascular, and the joints above and below."

- **Whole general/gait exam (video):** [▶ Dr James Gill (GALS) · 5:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5qJaf7gW-B0)

### The route on one page
| Step | What you do (in order) |
|---|---|
| Opening | IPEEP: introduce, permission, expose, explain; keep privacy |
| Clues | walking aid, appliance, footwear |
| General | conscious, oriented, comfortable; build; stigmata of disease |
| Standing | Look from front, side, behind, other side · posture |
| Walking | gait: up and back three times |
| Couch | Look · Feel · Move · Measure · Special |
| Finish | Neuro · Vascular · Joints above/below · lymph nodes |

- **Memory:** the 8 words — **Look, Feel, Move, Measure, Special, Neuro, Vascular, Joints above/below**

### Opening — IPEEP
| Letter | Do |
|---|---|
| I | "I am Dr X; I am going to examine you" |
| P | ask permission — here or abroad, always |
| E | expose both limbs; extent depends on the region |
| E | explain each step as you do it |

- The course spells out four letters; the last P is not named
- It then adds: respect privacy and culture (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Expose fully, yet keep the patient's dignity (Exam Techniques)

- Say: "If you start to feel pain, please stop me"
[[FIG: Fig 1.1 — Introduce yourself; watch the face throughout · 1.02

#### Equipment
- Tape measure, goniometer, tendon hammer; pin, pen, key and coin
[[FIG: Fig 1.2 — Basic equipment: goniometers, pen, key, coin, tape, hammer · 1.02

### Clues — before you touch
- **Memory:** three clues — **aid, appliance, shoe**

| Clue | Look for |
|---|---|
| Walking aid | stick, crutches, wheelchair |
| Appliance | brace, splint, prosthesis under the bed |
| Footwear | surgical shoe, heel raise, arch support, wear pattern |

- Missed clue, not commented on → marks lost (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Sole worn inside → overpronator; worn outside → underpronator (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Shoe raise of 5–6 cm → leg length discrepancy
[[FIG: Fig 1.3 — Footwear clues: sole wear and heel raise · 1.02

### General examination
| Say | Check |
|---|---|
| "Conscious, alert and stable" | general condition |
| "Oriented to time, person and place" | mental state |
| "Lying comfortably in bed" | pain, distress |
| "Average build and mentality" | habitus, weight |

- Stigmata: blue sclera, café-au-lait spots, multiple exostoses
- Scars must match the operations in the history

### Local examination — the rules
- Patient on a firm flat couch; start with the sound side; compare
- Finish every item in one position before the next (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Position order: standing, walking, sitting, supine, side-lying, prone

#### Look
| Look for | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Swelling — in or beyond the joint | effusion, pus, blood; or infection, tumour |
| Localized swelling | its anatomy names it, e.g. ganglion |
| Bruising, oedema | trauma, infection |
| Wasting | disuse, pain, denervation |
| Shape, posture, shortening | deformity, old trauma, joint destruction |
| Scars | injury or surgery |

- **Memory:** at every view **DCS** — deformity, contour and wasting, skin (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Say "attitude", not deformity, until you have examined it (Kasr Al-Ainy)

[[FIG: Fig 1.4 — Swelling confined to the joint, beyond it, localized · 1.02
[[FIG: Fig 1.5 — Bruising, wasting, alteration of shape · 1.02

#### Feel
- Warm your hands; watch the face as you palpate

| Feel | Means |
|---|---|
| Diffuse warmth | inflammation or infection |
| Localized warmth | the structure below |
| Cold limb | impaired circulation; feel both sides together |

- Find the point of maximal tenderness
[[FIG: Fig 1.6 — Feel for heat, then tenderness · 1.02

#### Move
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Demonstrate | the patient copies you |
| Active first | passive if active is limited |
| Record degrees | goniometer; compare the other side |
| Stop at pain | "painfully limited" is not "limited" (Kasr Al-Ainy) |
| Watch | trick movements; gravity helping a weak muscle |
| Feel | crepitus, clicks, abnormal planes |

[[FIG: Fig 1.7 — Range with a goniometer; abnormal planes; crepitus · 1.02

#### Measure and special tests
- Measure: lengths (→ ch 7), girth (1.4), angles (1.3)
- Special tests belong to each region (→ ch 2–12)

### Finish — Neuro, Vascular, Joints above/below
| Word | Do |
|---|---|
| Neuro | power proximal to distal, MRC grade; sensation, reflexes → ch 5, ch 9 |
| Vascular | pulses below the lesion; colour, warmth |
| Joints above/below | SUFE (slipped upper femoral epiphysis) presents with knee pain |
| Hidden areas | groin, perineum, regional lymph nodes |
[[FIG: Fig 1.8 — Sensory testing and mapping the area · 1.02

### Exam conduct
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Do not hurt the patient | pain ends the station |
| Be systematic | the commonest failure |
| No conclusion before the end | summary only at the end |
| Clear, concise summary | the examiner listens for order |

- The examiner judges your practice in the first 30 seconds (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Answer the request: whole exam or one step
- **Memory:** "**H**urt none, **S**ystem first, **S**ummary last"

PITFALL — "going back to standing after the couch"
- Returning for a missed standing test looks unsystematic (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Say → "**I have finished standing; now I will examine the patient supine.**"

1.03.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "describe this normal gait"
- "Walks unassisted, symmetrical gait, smooth transition from swing clearance to stance stability, adequate step length." (Kasr Al-Ainy)

### The gait cycle
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Gait cycle (stride) | heel strike to the next heel strike of the same foot |
| Step | initial contact of one foot to that of the other |
| Stance phase | foot on the ground — 60% |
| Swing phase | foot in the air — 40% |
| Double support | both feet down — 20–30% (Miller) |
| Cadence | steps per minute: 90–120 in adults (Hoppenfeld) |

- **Memory:** a stride = two steps = one cycle
[[FIG: Fig 1.9 — Stance phase, then swing phase · 1.03

#### The phases — old and new names
| Phase | Classic name | Modern name |
|---|---|---|
| Stance | heel strike | initial contact |
| Stance | foot flat | loading response |
| Stance | midstance | midstance |
| Stance | push-off | terminal stance, pre-swing |
| Swing | acceleration | initial swing |
| Swing | midswing | midswing |
| Swing | deceleration | terminal swing |

- **Memory:** **4 + 3** — four stance phases, three swing phases

#### Normal numbers
| Measure | Normal |
|---|---|
| Base width | 2–4 inches, heel to heel |
| Step length | about 15 inches |
| Centre of gravity | 2 cm in front of S2 (Miller) |
| Vertical rise of the centre | about 2 inches |

[[FIG: Fig 1.10 — Centre of gravity rises and falls about 2 inches · 1.03

#### Types of support
| Support | When |
|---|---|
| Double | both feet on the ground (walking) |
| Single | one foot on the ground |
| None | running only |

### Watching the walk
- Describe scientifically, never "fine"
- Watch aid, foot progression angle, heel strike, knee in stance and swing

### Abnormal gaits
| Gait | What you see | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| **Antalgic** | short stance on the painful leg | pain from sole to hip |
| **Trendelenburg** | opposite (lifted) side drops; trunk lurches over the hip | abductor failure |
| **Waddling** | lurch to both sides, duck-like | bilateral DDH, coxa vara, myopathy |
| **Short-limb** | shoulder dips on the short side in stance | leg length discrepancy |
| **High-stepping** | knee lifted high; foot slaps | foot drop |
| **Spastic, scissoring** | equinus, flexed knees and hips; legs cross | cerebral palsy |
| **Ataxic** | broad base, irregular, cannot walk heel-to-toe | cerebellar, sensory loss |
| **Gluteus maximus lurch** | trunk thrown back in stance | weak hip extensors |
| **Quadriceps (hand-to-knee)** | hand pushes thigh back; knee locks back | weak quadriceps, polio |

- **Memory:** stance causes = **W-I-P-F** — weak, unstable, painful, fused (Hoppenfeld)
- **Memory:** dip = short limb; lurch = unstable hip (Nagah)

#### Waddling gait

#### Short-limb gait

#### High-stepping (foot-drop) gait
- Causes: peroneal nerve, nerve root, hereditary neuropathy
[[FIG: Fig 1.15 — Toe scrape, steppage, foot slap · 1.03

#### Spastic and scissoring gait
- Adductor overactivity and internal rotation make the legs cross
- Toe walking with raised tone → think cerebral diplegia

#### Ataxic gait
- Base wider than 4 inches → suspect pathology (Hoppenfeld)
- Romberg test → ch 9
[[FIG: Fig 1.16 — Normal base 2–4 inches; step about 15 inches · 1.03

#### Gluteus maximus lurch
- Trunk thrown back keeps the hip extended in stance
[[FIG: Fig 1.17 — Extensor (gluteus maximus) lurch · 1.03

#### Quadriceps (hand-to-knee) gait
- Weak quadriceps: the knee buckles at heel strike
[[FIG: Fig 1.18 — Hand pushes the knee into extension · 1.03

#### Other gaits
| Gait | Point |
|---|---|
| Fused hip | pelvis and spine swing the leg |
| Stiff knee | hip hiked or leg circumducted to clear the floor |
| Calcaneus (flat-foot) | weak calf: no push-off |
| Toe walking | tight heel cord; early Duchenne dystrophy |
| Crouch | weak calf: ankles dorsiflexed, knees bent |
| Shuffling | Parkinsonism |
| Stooped | lumbar canal stenosis → ch 9 |

[[FIG: Fig 1.19 — Fused hip; hip hiking with a fused knee · 1.03

### Range of motion
- Zero = the anatomic position; measure with a goniometer
- Compare the sound side; both affected → normal ranges
- Write the number and whether it was painful

#### Recording a deformity
| Finding | Write |
|---|---|
| Cannot reach neutral (straight) | fixed deformity, e.g. 20° fixed flexion deformity (FFD) |
| Range from the deformity | "20° FFD, flexes to 110°" |
| Active and passive extension lost | fixed flexion deformity |
| Active extension lost, passive full | extension lag |
| Abduction fails to reach neutral | abduction deformity, not "adduction 20°" |

- FFD versus lag: both active and passive lost, or active only (Nagah)
[[FIG: Fig 1.20 — Genu valgum and genu varum · 1.03

#### Varus or valgus?
- Valgus: the distal segment points away from the midline
- Varus: the distal segment points toward the midline
- Example: genu valgum — knees touch, ankles apart

PITFALL — "calling every limp antalgic"
- First divide antalgic from non-antalgic, then name it
- Say → "**Non-antalgic gait: the opposite (lifted) side drops — a Trendelenburg gait.**"

1.03.4.b:
- Zero = the anatomic position; measure with a goniometer
- Compare the sound side; both affected → normal ranges
- Write the number and whether it was painful

#### Recording a deformity
| Finding | Write |
|---|---|
| Cannot reach neutral (straight) | fixed deformity, e.g. 20° fixed flexion deformity (FFD) |
| Range from the deformity | "20° FFD, flexes to 110°" |
| Active and passive extension lost | fixed flexion deformity |
| Active extension lost, passive full | extension lag |
| Abduction fails to reach neutral | abduction deformity, not "adduction 20°" |

- FFD versus lag: both active and passive lost, or active only (Nagah)
[[FIG: Fig 1.20 — Genu valgum and genu varum · 1.03

#### Varus or valgus?
- Valgus: the distal segment points away from the midline
- Varus: the distal segment points toward the midline
- Example: genu valgum — knees touch, ankles apart

PITFALL — "calling every limp antalgic"
- First divide antalgic from non-antalgic, then name it
- Say → "**Non-antalgic gait: the opposite (lifted) side drops — a Trendelenburg gait.**"

1.04.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "the general stations"
- "Describe a gait, measure with a goniometer, grade power, score hyperlaxity."
- "Measure girth, and look for Gowers sign in a weak child."

### "Describe this gait"
#### Gait description
- **Aim:** describe walking scientifically in one sentence
- **How:** patient walks up and back three times; watch front, side, behind
- **Positive:** asymmetry → name the gait from the 1.3 table
- **Why:** most problems appear when the limb takes weight
- **Video:** [▶ USMLE pass · 2:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nmSEtrn_T5A)

[[FIG: Fig 1.21 — Normal gait cycle, one foot followed · 1.04

### "Measure this joint"
#### Goniometer measurement
- **Aim:** joint range in degrees
- **How:** hinge over the joint axis; arms along the two segments
- **Positive:** cannot reach zero → fixed deformity; below sound side → limitation
- **Why:** numbers compare sides and visits
- **Video:** [▶ YourOrthoMD · 1:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7mAFp8VkQs)

[[FIG: Fig 1.22 — Goniometer aligned with the limb segments · 1.04

### "Test the power"
#### MRC power grading
- **Aim:** grade muscle power 0–5
- **How:** patient moves against gravity, then against your resistance
- **Positive:** fails against gravity → retest gravity eliminated (grade 2 or less)
- **Why:** separates grade 3 from grade 2
- **Trap:** grade 4 = weaker than the other side (Reider)
- **Video:** [▶ MSK Medicine · 2:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LUehNRVykIM)

[[FIG: Fig 1.23 — Quadriceps against gravity; then gravity eliminated, side-lying · 1.04

| Grade | Movement |
|---|---|
| 5 | normal power |
| 4 | against gravity and some resistance |
| 3 | against gravity, no resistance |
| 2 | only with gravity eliminated |
| 1 | flicker of contraction |
| 0 | no contraction |

- **Memory:** MRC (Medical Research Council): 3 = gravity in; 2 = gravity out

#### Gowers sign
- **Aim:** proximal (hip girdle) weakness in a child
- **How:** child rises from the floor; you watch the hands
- **Positive:** hands climb up the thighs → proximal myopathy, e.g. Duchenne
- **Why:** the arms replace weak proximal muscles
- **Video:** [▶ Heafner Health PT · 0:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOQ9TFwMIc4)

[[FIG: Fig 1.24 — Gowers sign: climbing up the legs to stand · 1.04

### "Is this patient hyperlax?"
#### Beighton score
- **Aim:** generalized joint hypermobility
- **How:** each side: little finger >90°, thumb to forearm, elbow, knee
- **How:** plus palms flat to the floor
- **Positive:** 4 or more of 9 → hypermobile (Exam Techniques)
- **Why:** laxity changes instability surgery and its results
- **Trap:** 5 or more; elbow and knee count beyond 10° (Miller)
- **Video:** [▶ Shane Robinson · 2:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uYRYsCW0gI8)

[[FIG: Fig 1.25 — Beighton score items; tests of ligamentous laxity · 1.04

- Do it standing, before the supine tests
- **Memory:** 4 pairs + 1 back = 9 points

### "Is the limb wasted?"
#### Limb circumference
- **Aim:** muscle wasting, measured
- **How:** mark both thighs equally from a landmark; tape round each
- **Positive:** 1 cm or more less → significant atrophy (Reider)
- **Why:** wasting follows pain, disuse or denervation
- **Trap:** same point on both sides
- **Video:** [▶ Ontario Tech Kinesiology · 0:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-MOfNPNXZfc)

[[FIG: Fig 1.26 — Thigh girth at a marked level · 1.04

### Other tests
| Test | Point |
|---|---|
| Romberg | sways with eyes closed → posterior columns (→ ch 9) |
| Trendelenburg | abductor mechanism (→ ch 7) |
| True and apparent length | tape from ASIS (anterior superior iliac spine) or xiphisternum (→ ch 7) |
| Sensation, two-point discrimination | → ch 4 and ch 5 |
| Height, span, sitting height | short stature: proportionate or not |

PITFALL — "a Beighton score from the knees alone"
- One hyperextended knee is not hyperlaxity; score all 9 points
- Say → "**Beighton 6 of 9: generalized hypermobility.**"

1.05.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "the general spot diagnosis"
- "Spot the whole patient: height, proportions, eyes, skin, limbs."
- "Do two checks; say one diagnosis and one differential."

### Achondroplasia
- **Spot:** short limbs, normal trunk, bossed forehead, flat nasal bridge
- **Do:** trident hands; fingertips reach only the trochanters
- **Do:** bowed legs, lumbar lordosis; ask about claudication (stenosis)
- **Say:** "Achondroplasia, short-limbed dwarfism. Differential: pseudoachondroplasia."

[[FIG: Fig 1.27 — Achondroplasia; genu valgum in pseudoachondroplasia · 1.05

### Osteogenesis imperfecta
- **Spot:** short, bowed limbs, blue sclerae
- **Do:** teeth (dentinogenesis imperfecta), hearing, lax joints, scoliosis
- **Do:** femur bows anterolaterally; tibia anteriorly
- **Say:** "Osteogenesis imperfecta. Differential: non-accidental injury."

[[FIG: Fig 1.28 — Blue sclerae; amber, translucent teeth · 1.05

### Neurofibromatosis type 1
- **Spot:** café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, axillary freckling
- **Do:** count spots: 6 or more, >1.5 cm after puberty (Campbell)
- **Do:** spine (short sharp scoliosis), tibial bowing, limb length
- **Say:** "Neurofibromatosis type 1. Differential: McCune-Albright syndrome."

[[FIG: Fig 1.29 — Café-au-lait spots · 1.05

### Marfan syndrome and hyperlaxity
- **Spot:** tall, long slender fingers, pectus deformity
- **Do:** thumb sign — thumb beyond the ulnar border in the fist
- **Do:** wrist sign — thumb overlaps the little finger round the wrist
- **Say:** "Marfan syndrome. Differential: homocystinuria."

[[FIG: Fig 1.30 — Marfan habitus: scoliosis, chest deformity, slender build · 1.05

- Hyperlax, not tall → Beighton score (1.4); think Ehlers-Danlos
- Marfan lens dislocates up; homocystinuria down

### Polio sequelae
- **Spot:** thin, short, wasted limb; hand-to-knee gait
- **Do:** MRC grade each group; sensation is normal
- **Do:** deformities — equinus is the commonest (Nagah); leg length
- **Say:** "Post-polio residual paralysis, left lower limb. Differential: spinal muscular atrophy."

### Hereditary multiple exostoses
- **Spot:** bony lumps near the knees, short limbs, bowed forearm
- **Do:** count the lumps, nerve pressure; malignant change → ch 12
- **Say:** "Hereditary multiple exostoses. Differential: solitary osteochondroma."

[[FIG: Fig 1.31 — Diaphyseal aclasis: short limbs, knee swellings, chest mass · 1.05

PITFALL — "looking only at the limb you were shown"
- Dysplasias are whole-body diseases: look at face, eyes, skin, hands, spine
- Say → "**Short-limbed, with frontal bossing and trident hands — achondroplasia.**"

1.06.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "present your case"
- "Personal data, complaint, present and past history; general, then local findings."
- "Then site, pathology and function — and what I would do next."

### Present it like this (course case 1)
| Part | Say |
|---|---|
| Personal | "Mr X, 52, married, manual worker, smoker." |
| Complaint | "Bilateral hip pain, left worse, for 2 years." |
| Present | "Insidious, progressive; worse walking and stairs; eased by rest." |
| Past, drugs | "Rheumatoid arthritis for 6 years; steroids." |
| General | "Conscious, oriented, stable; average build." |
| Local | "Antalgic gait with a stick; findings standing, then supine." |
| Verdict | "Intra-articular disease of both hips; I would image and examine the spine." |

### The diagnosis in four steps
| Step | Ask yourself |
|---|---|
| Site | which structure? Joint or around it? |
| Pathology | which group? |
| Function | how much disability? |
| Plan | what can be done? |

- Limitation in all directions with FFD → intra-articular disease (Kasr Al-Ainy)

#### Differential by pathology
| Group | Examples |
|---|---|
| Metabolic | rickets, osteomalacia |
| Inflammatory, infective | RA, septic arthritis, tuberculosis (TB) |
| Neoplastic | primary tumour, metastasis |
| Degenerative | osteoarthritis |
| Congenital | dysplasia, DDH |
| Traumatic | old fracture, malunion |

- **Memory:** **MIND the CT** — metabolic, inflammatory, neoplastic, degenerative, congenital, traumatic

### "What investigations?"
| Ask for | Why |
|---|---|
| Plain X-ray, two views | first and always |
| ESR, CRP | infection, inflammation |
| Full blood count | infection, anaemia |
| Rheumatoid factor | rheumatoid disease |
| Calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase | metabolic bone disease |
| Uric acid | gout |
| Chest X-ray | tumour, TB |

- ESR = erythrocyte sedimentation rate; CRP = C-reactive protein
- Then CT, MRI, scan — chosen by the clinical question

### How to read an X-ray
| Shot | Look at |
|---|---|
| Long shot | whole film: which bones, one side or both |
| Medium shot | bone shape, size, contour; joint alignment |
| Close-up | texture, new bone, destruction, joint space |

- **Memory:** read like a film — **long shot, medium shot, close-up** (McRae)
- Pelvis view → both sides; hip view → detail
- Extra films: comparison, oblique, localized, stress

[[FIG: Fig 1.32 — Describe the film; then CT showed bilateral cysts · 1.06

### The Examiner Asks
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Stance and swing share? | 60% and 40% |
| Dip versus lurch? | dip = short limb; lurch = unstable hip |
| Stick in which hand? | opposite hand (hip) |
| MRC 2 versus 3? | gravity eliminated versus against gravity |
| Beighton positive? | 4 or more of 9 |
| Why active before passive? | shows the useful, pain-free range |
| Why examine the joint above? | referred pain: SUFE with knee pain |
| Hallmark of polio? | weakness with normal sensation |
| ROM in a fused joint? | none, active or passive |

PITFALL — "naming the disease from the X-ray first"
- Imaging seen first pulls you toward a finding unrelated to the complaint
- Say → "**On the film I see… Clinically this fits…**"
